hook.situation: You are in a clothing store, want to try on a shirt, ask for a different size, choose something neat for an interview, and check whether exchange or refund is possible.
objectives: Use clothing words with 입다, 신다, 사이즈가 맞다, and 잘 어울리다.
Ask store staff politely with 입어 봐도 돼요? and 보여 주시겠어요?
Describe appearance and interview appropriateness with 커 보여요, 단정해 보여요, and N보다 더 A.
hook.whyItMatters: This chapter should not be a random clothing list. The vocabulary has to serve one real flow: try on clothes, judge fit and style, compare options, and confirm store policy before buying.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어 보세요 — try doing it
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when someone suggests trying an action once before deciding. In clothing stores, the key action is 입어 보다: try it on.
grammarNotes.formation: Make the 아/어 form of the verb and add 보다. 입다 becomes 입어 보다, 신다 becomes 신어 보다, and 해 보다 is used for 하다 verbs. 보세요 is a polite suggestion; 봐도 돼요? asks permission to try.

examples.en: May I try on this shirt?
May I try on these sneakers too?

examples.ko: 한 치수 작은 것도 입어 보세요.
examples.romanization: han chisu jageun geotdo ibeo boseyo.
examples.en: Try on one size smaller too.
Make sure you try on a coat before buying it.

exceptions: 입어 보다 is for trying on clothes. 신어 보다 is for shoes. Do not use 입다 for shoes.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어 주시겠어요? — could you please do it for me?
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this for a polite store request when the staff member has to do something for you.
grammarNotes.formation: Make the 아/어 form, add 주시겠어요? 보여 주시겠어요? asks someone to show you something. 교환해 주시겠어요? asks them to exchange it for you. It is softer than a direct 주세요.

examples.ko: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
examples.romanization: han chisu jageun geotdo boyeo jusigesseoyo?
examples.en: Could you show me one size smaller too?
Could you show me another color too?
examples.note: A color request in a store.

examples.en: Could you exchange it for this one?
Could you put the receipt in too?

exceptions: 주세요 is fine for simple buying. 주시겠어요? is better when you are asking for effort, checking stock, or making a favor-like request.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-아/어 보이다 — it looks / appears
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when you judge how clothing appears, not whether the size technically fits.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -아/어 보이다 to a descriptive stem. 크다 becomes 커 보여요, 작다 becomes 작아 보여요, 단정하다 becomes 단정해 보여요, and 비싸다 becomes 비싸 보여요.

examples.en: It looks a little big.
examples.note: Appearance judgment before asking another size.

examples.en: The navy shirt looks neater.
This coat looks expensive.
examples.note: Looks expensive, not necessarily is expensive.

examples.en: That color makes your face look bright.

exceptions: 커 보여요 means it looks big. 사이즈가 커요 says the size is big. 사이즈가 맞아요 says it fits.

grammarNotes.title: A-ㄴ/은 N — adjective before a clothing noun
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this compact form when comparing clothes by fit, color, style, or occasion.
grammarNotes.formation: For many adjective stems, add -ㄴ after a vowel and -은 after a consonant: 단정하다 -> 단정한, 작다 -> 작은, 크다 -> 큰. Irregulars appear often in clothing, such as 가볍다 -> 가벼운.

examples.en: a neat shirt
one size smaller
comfortable sneakers
a light coat

grammarNotes.title: N보다 더 A — more A than N
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Use this when choosing between two clothes, colors, or sizes.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 보다 to the comparison baseline, then use 더 plus an adjective. 이 셔츠보다 남색 셔츠가 더 단정해 보여요 means the navy shirt is the one that looks neater.

examples.ko: 이 셔츠보다 남색 셔츠가 더 단정해 보여요.
examples.romanization: i syeocheuboda namsaek syeocheuga deo danjeonghae boyeoyo.
examples.en: The navy shirt looks neater than this shirt.
Dress shoes look more presentable than sneakers.

examples.ko: 이 색깔보다 남색이 더 잘 어울려요.
examples.romanization: i saekkkalboda namsaegi deo jal eoullyeoyo.
examples.en: Navy suits you better than this color.
examples.note: 어울리다 is style harmony, not size fit.

examples.ko: 이 사이즈보다 한 치수 작은 게 더 맞아요.
examples.romanization: i saijeuboda han chisu jageun ge deo majayo.
examples.en: One size smaller fits better than this size.

exceptions: 보다 attaches to the thing you compare against. Do not attach it to the item you are recommending.

exampleSentence.en: May I try on this shirt?
I often wear T-shirts in summer.
The pants look a little big.
These dress shoes go well with the skirt.

exampleSentence.ko: 이 원피스는 면접에는 조금 화려해 보여요.
exampleSentence.en: This dress looks a little flashy for an interview.
May I try on these sneakers too?

exampleSentence.ko: 면접에는 운동화보다 구두가 더 단정해 보여요.
exampleSentence.en: For an interview, dress shoes look more presentable than sneakers.
Could you show me another color too?
For an interview, a navy shirt looks neat and presentable.

exampleSentence.ko: 사이즈가 조금 커서 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
exampleSentence.en: The size is a little big, so could you show me one size smaller too?

exampleSentence.ko: 한 치수 작은 것도 입어 봐도 돼요?
exampleSentence.en: May I try on one size smaller too?
The fitting room is on the right.

extendedVocabulary.english: to suit; to look good on

exampleSentence.note: Linked to dictionary card word-ext-1971 and expression expr-765.

exampleSentence.en: Can I get a refund too?
exampleSentence.note: Linked to dictionary card word-ext-143 and expression expr-764.

exampleSentence.en: For an interview, a neat shirt is good.

extendedDialogue.setting: A shopper tries on a shirt, asks for another size, and chooses an interview outfit.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: May I try on this shirt?
lines.grammarNote: -아/어 봐도 돼요 asks permission to try an action.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, the fitting room is on the right.
lines.grammarNote: 피팅룸 is the store-location word connected to trying on.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 조금 커 보여요. 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
lines.romanization: jogeum keo boyeoyo. han chisu jageun geotdo boyeo jusigesseoyo?
lines.en: It looks a little big. Could you show me one size smaller too?
lines.grammarNote: 커 보여요 is appearance; 한 치수 작은 거 is the size request.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네. 면접에는 이 셔츠보다 남색 셔츠가 더 단정해 보여요.
lines.romanization: ne. myeonjeobeneun i syeocheuboda namsaek syeocheuga deo danjeonghae boyeoyo.
lines.en: Sure. For an interview, the navy shirt looks neater than this shirt.
lines.grammarNote: 이 셔츠보다 gives the comparison baseline, and 더 단정해 보여요 describes the appearance.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ko: 그럼 이걸로 할게요. 교환이나 환불도 돼요?
lines.romanization: geureom igeollo halgeyo. gyohwanina hwanbuldo dwaeyo?
lines.en: Then I'll take this one. Can I exchange or refund it too?
lines.grammarNote: 교환/환불이 되다 asks about store policy.

readingText.title: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
readingText.body: 민서는 면접에 입을 셔츠를 사러 갔어요. 먼저 직원에게 '이 셔츠 입어 봐도 돼요?'라고 물었어요. 피팅룸에서 입어 보니 사이즈가 조금 커 보였어요. 그래서 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 달라고 했어요. 직원은 면접에는 이 셔츠보다 남색 셔츠가 더 단정해 보인다고 말했어요. 민서는 그 셔츠가 잘 어울리고 사이즈도 맞아서 샀어요. 마지막으로 교환이나 환불이 되는지도 확인했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo went to buy a shirt for an interview. First, Minseo asked a staff member if trying on the shirt was allowed. After trying it on in the fitting room, the size looked a little big, so Minseo asked to see one size smaller. The staff member said a navy shirt looked neater for an interview. It suited Minseo and the size fit, so Minseo bought it. Finally, Minseo checked whether exchange or refund was possible.

culturalNote.title: Fit, style, and policy are separate questions
culturalNote.body: In a Korean clothing store, keep three questions separate. First, size: 사이즈가 맞아요? 한 치수 작은 거 있어요? Second, style: 잘 어울려요? 단정해 보여요? Third, policy: 교환돼요? 환불돼요? Learners often mix these because English can say 'it works' for all three, but Korean uses different verbs.
culturalNote.tip: For clothes, 입다 is for clothing and 신다 is for shoes. For compliments, the clothing or color is the subject: 이 옷이 잘 어울려요, not 이 옷을 잘 어울려요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence asks permission to try on a shirt?
inlineExercises.explanation: 입다 is for clothing, and -아/어 봐도 돼요? asks permission.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence asks for one size smaller politely?
options: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
한 치수 작은 것도 먹어 보세요?
한 치수 작은 것도 잘 어울려요?
inlineExercises.correct: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주시겠어요?
inlineExercises.explanation: 보여 주시겠어요? is a polite request to staff.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence is about style, not size?
inlineExercises.explanation: 어울리다 describes whether something suits someone. 맞다 is about fit.

inlineExercises.prompt: Complete: 면접에는 남색 셔츠가 더 단정해 ___.

bullets: Core flow: try on clothing, ask for another size, compare appearance, then check exchange/refund.
Use 입다 for clothes and 신다 for shoes.
맞다 is size fit, 어울리다 is style harmony, and 단정해 보이다 is presentable appearance.
Use 보여 주시겠어요? for polite staff requests and N보다 더 A for comparing options.
